original_record.question:
Suppose we have a hexagonal grid in the shape of a hexagon of side length $4$ as shown at left. Define a “chunk” to be four tiles, two of which are adjacent to the other three, and the other two of which are adjacent to just two of the others. The three possible rotations of these are shown at right.

In how many ways can we choose a chunk from the grid?
<image1>
original_record.solution: Call a hexagon (hex) a "centerpiece" of a chunk if it is in one of the two chunk's hexes adjacent to all the other hexes in the chunk. If we sum over all hexes the number of chunks that the hex is a centerpiece of, we will clearly get twice the number of chunks. Each corner is a centerpiece of only one, each edge is a centerpiece of two, and each middle piece is a centerpiece of six. Since there are 19 middle pieces, 12 edge pieces, and 6 corner pieces, this gives $144 / 2=72$ chunks.
